claims.text: Ultrasonic vibration-assisted deposition improves the wear resistance of HEA protective coatings.
The wear improvement from ultrasonic assistance is mediated by an increase in the H³/Er² ratio.
Microstructural refinement and densification caused by ultrasonic assistance enhance the H³/Er² ratio.
Conventional coatings may contain larger grains or greater porosity than ultrasonically assisted coatings.
An ultrasonic amplitude around 5 µm is optimal for improving coating properties and wear performance.
Ultrasonic vibration introduces acoustic and cavitation effects during deposition.
Acoustic and cavitation effects promote grain refinement.
Acoustic and cavitation effects reduce coating defects and produce a denser coating.
Ultrasonic assistance increases coating hardness more than it increases reduced elastic modulus.
A higher H³/Er² ratio predicts improved resistance to abrasive and adhesive wear.
Coatings deposited with approximately 5 µm ultrasonic amplitude will have a higher H³/Er² ratio than conventionally deposited coatings.
Coatings deposited with approximately 5 µm ultrasonic amplitude will have lower wear-scar depth than conventional coatings.
Coatings deposited with approximately 5 µm ultrasonic amplitude will have a lower friction coefficient than conventional coatings.
Coatings deposited with approximately 5 µm ultrasonic amplitude will exhibit improved overall wear performance.
Conventionally deposited coatings have lower H³/Er² ratios than ultrasonically assisted coatings.
Conventionally deposited coatings have poorer wear resistance, including higher friction and deeper wear scars.
The expected ultrasonic effect applies when composition, temperature, substrate conditions, and other deposition parameters are held constant.
Increasing ultrasonic amplitude substantially above 5 µm produces diminishing improvement or possible degradation.
The quantitative changes in H³/Er² and wear resistance depend on deposition conditions and HEA composition.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant H³/Er² increase together with improved wear metrics would falsify the proposed mechanism.
